scenes.title: The Captain Takes Lodging
scenes.summary: Jim Hawkins introduces himself writing for Squire Trelawney and Doctor Livesey, then recalls the arrival of a scarred old seaman at the Admiral Benbow Inn who pays in gold, claims the lookout berth, and calls himself captain.

scenes.title: Watch for the One-Legged Man
scenes.summary: The captain watches the coast with his telescope, shuns other seamen, and bribes Jim to keep watch for a seafaring man with one leg, a figure who soon haunts Jim's nightmares.

scenes.title: Wild Songs and Dreadful Stories
scenes.summary: Drunk on rum the captain tyrannizes the parlor, forcing the trembling company to join his wild sea-songs and listen to dreadful stories of hanging, walking the plank, and the Spanish Main, frightening the neighbors even as the younger men admire him as a true seadog.

scenes.title: Unpaid Score and Unopened Chest
scenes.summary: The captain stays week after week and month after month long after his money is exhausted, roaring at and staring down Jim's father whenever payment is mentioned and hastening his unhappy decline, while changing nothing but stockings, patching his coat to rags, writing no letters, and keeping his great sea-chest forever unopened.

scenes.title: The Doctor Faces Down the Captain
scenes.summary: When Doctor Livesey visits the ailing landlord, the captain demands silence for his song and draws his knife, but Livesey calmly threatens him with hanging as magistrate and warns he will be watched, cowing him into quiet.

muse_override.reason: Tense tavern standoff where calm authority stares down a drunken knife threat.

scenes.title: Winter Gloom at the Inn
scenes.summary: A bitter winter settles over the inn as Jim's father sinks toward death. The captain rises early and strides off down the frosty cove, leaving Jim to lay breakfast.

scenes.title: The Stranger Waits in Ambush
scenes.summary: A pale, two-fingers-missing stranger enters asking for rum and for mate Bill. He questions Jim about the captain's movements, then bullies Jim into hiding with him behind the parlor door to spring a surprise.

scenes.title: Bill Meets Black Dog
scenes.summary: The captain returns and is stunned to face his old shipmate. Color drains from him at the name Black Dog, and the two uneasily agree to talk square over rum.

scenes.title: Rum Talk Turns to Steel
scenes.summary: Left alone with the door open, the sailors mutter then shout oaths about swinging. Talk erupts into a clash of cutlasses, ending with Black Dog fleeing wounded and the captain slashing the inn signboard.

scenes.title: Flight and Collapse
scenes.summary: Black Dog escapes over the hill while the bewildered captain staggers inside demanding rum. He collapses full-length on the parlor floor, breathing hard with closed eyes and horrible color.

scenes.title: The Doctor's Warning
scenes.summary: Doctor Livesey arrives and declares it a stroke from drink, not a wound. He bleeds the tattooed captain back to consciousness and sternly warns that rum is death, before ordering a week of bed rest.

scenes.title: A Noggin of Rum
scenes.summary: At noon Jim visits the sick captain, who pleads desperately for rum despite the doctor's orders. Excited and trembling, he offers a bribe, but Jim agrees to bring only one glass.

scenes.title: Flint's First Mate Warns of the Black Spot
scenes.summary: Strengthened briefly by rum, the captain rages against his shipmates and fears the black spot. He confesses he was Flint's first mate and charges Jim to fetch the doctor and magistrates if the spot comes or one-legged man appears. Jim's father then dies suddenly, suspending all else.

scenes.title: The Weakened Captain in Mourning
scenes.summary: In the gloomy days after his father's death, Jim watches the weakened captain drift about the inn, drinking heavily, singing his sea-song and then a strange love-song, growing weaker, wandering, and frightening everyone with his drunken temper and drawn cutlass.

scenes.title: The Blind Beggar on the Road
scenes.summary: The afternoon after the funeral, on a bitter foggy afternoon, Jim stands at the door thinking of his father when a dreadful blind beggar in a green shade and tattered sea-cloak taps up the road, chanting for directions to the Admiral Benbow, which Jim gives him.

scenes.title: Led in by Force
scenes.summary: The blind man seizes Jim's hand in a vise-like grip and threatens to break his arm unless he is led straight to the captain. Terrified by the cruel voice and wrenching pain, Jim drags him into the parlor to deliver a 'friend for Bill.'

scenes.title: Business Is Business
scenes.summary: The rum leaves the captain sober with mortal sickness at the sight of his visitor. Held fast, Jim brings the captain's left hand to the beggar, who drops the summons into his palm and vanishes with uncanny nimbleness down the road.

muse_override.reason: Blind beggar's cold ritual and secret handoff create tense mystery as captain sickens.

scenes.title: Ten O'Clock - Death
scenes.summary: The captain reads the spot: ten o'clock, six hours left. He leaps up vowing they will escape yet, then reels, clutches his throat, and falls dead of apoplexy as Jim runs for his mother and weeps over the second death in days.

scenes.title: Panic and a Plea for Help
scenes.summary: Terrified alone in the inn with the captain's corpse and fearing his shipmates' return, Jim tells his mother everything and they flee through fog to the hamlet for help, only to find the villagers too frightened by Captain Flint's name to defend the Admiral Benbow.

scenes.title: Mother's Defiance and the Dangerous Return
scenes.summary: Jim's mother shames the cowardly villagers into lending a pistol and sending for the doctor, then bravely leads Jim back through the moonlit fog to open the captain's chest and claim what they are owed.

scenes.title: Finding the Black Spot
scenes.summary: Locked in with the dead captain, Jim and his mother enter the parlor by candlelight and find the black spot beside his hand warning he has till ten tonight, while the clock striking six gives them hope, and his mother urges Jim to get the key.

scenes.title: Unlocking the Captain's Chest
scenes.summary: Jim finds the chest key hung round the captain's neck, and upstairs mother and son open the sea-chest to find clothes, quadrant, pistols, silver, trinkets, shells, papers, and a bag of gold, which she begins carefully counting to take only her dues.

muse_override.reason: Tense secret search of the dead captain's chest blending mystery, suspense and adventure toward gold.

scenes.title: Pursued in the Moonlight
scenes.summary: Counting is interrupted by the blind man's tapping at the door and a distant warning whistle; grabbing coins and the oilskin packet, they flee into the dispersing fog as pursuers with a lantern approach, until his collapsing mother forces Jim to drag her under the bridge to hide.

scenes.title: The Gang Storms the Inn
scenes.summary: Hiding behind broom by the road, Jim watches Pew and seven or eight men rush in. Pew orders them to break down the door of the Admiral Benbow.

scenes.title: Search, Loot, and Warning Whistle
scenes.summary: The pirates burst in to find Bill dead and the chest already rifled. Pew rages and orders them to search Jim and his mother, ransack the inn, then a warning whistle from the hamlet signals danger.

scenes.title: Pew Abandoned and Trampled
scenes.summary: Pew quarrels violently with his crew over the missing papers. Galloping revenue officers arrive, the pirates flee and abandon the blind man, who is trampled to death under the horses.

scenes.title: Rescue and the Ruined Inn
scenes.summary: Hailed by Jim, Supervisor Dance's riders explain they were alerted by news of the lugger in Kitt's Hole. Pew is found stone dead and Jim's mother is carried to the hamlet to recover. Dance fails to stop the escaping lugger and returns with Jim to the smashed Admiral Benbow, where Jim reveals he carries the thing the pirates sought in his breast-pocket.

scenes.title: Entrusting the Packet and Ride to the Doctor
scenes.summary: Dance agrees the packet must be put in safety and suggests Doctor Livesey as gentleman and magistrate, offering to ride there himself and take Jim along. After telling his mother, Jim mounts behind Dogger and the party trots off toward Doctor Livesey's house.

scenes.title: Night Ride to the Hall
scenes.summary: After hard night riding, Jim finds Doctor Livesey is not home and runs with the officers up the moonlit avenue to the Hall, where they are admitted to the library.

muse_override.reason: Urgent moonlit ride sustains suspense and adventure easing into warm library calm.

scenes.title: Tale by the Library Fire
scenes.summary: In the warm library, the squire and doctor hear Dance's breathless report of the attack, praise Jim and Dance, receive the oilskin packet, and give Jim supper while Dance is dismissed.

muse_override.reason: Warm fireside hospitality and excited storytelling spark joyful anticipation of adventure.

scenes.title: Dream of Flint's Treasure
scenes.summary: The doctor and the excitable squire discuss Captain Flint, the possibility of buried money, and the squire's instant resolve to fit out a ship from Bristol to seek it.

scenes.title: The Account-Book of Crimes
scenes.summary: They cut open the packet and puzzle over the captain's account-book of crosses, sums, bearings, and totals, which the squire explains as a record of plundered ships.

scenes.title: The Treasure Map Revealed
scenes.summary: Doctor Livesey opens the thimble-sealed paper to reveal a detailed map of a dragon-shaped island with harbors, soundings, and three red crosses marking treasure, delighting the squire and doctor despite its mystery to Jim.

scenes.title: The Vow of Silence
scenes.summary: Livesey warns that the inn's attackers and their confederates still seek the money, chides Trelawney for loose talk, and extracts a vow that none shall breathe a word or travel alone until they are at sea.

scenes.title: Sea-Dreams at the Hall
scenes.summary: Jim waits impatiently at the Hall under Redruth's guard while the squire and doctor prepare in Bristol and London, whiling away hours fantasizing over the treasure map and the island's hills, savages, and dangers.

scenes.title: The Squire's Letter from Bristol
scenes.summary: Jim opens Trelawney's long letter from Bristol announcing the purchased schooner Hispaniola, Blandly's help, and the fortuitous hiring of one-legged cook Long John Silver, who assembled a tough crew and officers, with orders for Jim and Redruth to hurry to Bristol.

scenes.title: Return to the Admiral Benbow
scenes.summary: Thrilled by the letter, Jim rejoices while Tom Redruth grumbles at being chosen, and next morning they walk to the Admiral Benbow where Jim finds his mother well, the captain dead, and the inn repaired and refurnished by the squire with an apprentice boy to help.

scenes.title: Tears and Farewell to the Cove
scenes.summary: Seeing the clumsy boy replacing him brings Jim's first tears and makes him harsh to the newcomer, then after a night he leaves with Redruth, sorrowfully bidding goodbye to his mother, the cove, and the repainted Benbow with a last thought of the captain.

scenes.title: Night Coach to Bristol
scenes.summary: Jim and Redruth take the mail coach across the heath, Jim dozing through the cold night stages until Redruth wakes him at dawn in the city streets of Bristol.

scenes.title: Arrival on the Quays
scenes.summary: Walking the crowded quays amid ships, tar smells, singing sailors, and figureheads, Jim revels in his dream of sailing for treasure, then meets the elated squire dressed as a sea officer who announces the doctor has arrived and they sail tomorrow.

scenes.title: Finding the Spy-glass
scenes.summary: Jim follows the busy docks to find the Spy-glass tavern, describing its bright, clean interior and loud seafaring crowd that makes him hesitate at the door.

scenes.title: Meeting Long John
scenes.summary: Long John Silver hops out on his crutch, cheerful and friendly; Jim decides he cannot be the Benbow buccaneer and delivers Squire Trelawney's note as the new cabin-boy.

muse_override.reason: Cheerful tavern welcome eases Jim's pirate fear as adventure begins with uneasy undercurrent.

scenes.title: Black Dog Escapes
scenes.summary: Jim spots Black Dog fleeing the tavern; Silver sends men in pursuit, angrily interrogates Morgan about talking with him, and performs outrage so convincingly that Jim's reawakened suspicions fade.

scenes.title: Silver Pleads His Helplessness
scenes.summary: Silver laments to Jim that he let Black Dog slip from his own house while drinking his rum, begs Jim to do him justice with Captain Trelawney, and blames his crippled leg for failing to seize him.

scenes.title: Laughing Over the Forgotten Score
scenes.summary: Silver suddenly remembers his forgotten rum score and bursts into roaring laughter that Jim joins, then wins Jim over on their walk along the quays, charming him with sailor lore about ships, rigs, cargoes, and sea phrases.

scenes.title: Report and Approval
scenes.summary: At the inn Silver truthfully recounts the affair to the squire and doctor, is complimented and trusted, and Jim is invited to come aboard to see the ship.

scenes.title: Boarding the Hispaniola
scenes.summary: Jim and the party row out and board the Hispaniola. They are greeted by mate Mr. Arrow, but Jim senses immediate friction between Squire Trelawney and the sharp, angry Captain Smollett.

scenes.title: The Captain's Blunt Complaint
scenes.summary: In the cabin the captain bluntly says he dislikes the cruise, the men, and his officer. Pressed by the doctor, he complains of sealed orders and that the treasure secret has been blabbed to everyone.

scenes.title: Demands for Precaution
scenes.summary: Questioned further, Smollett objects to the crew not of his choosing and to Mr. Arrow's over-familiarity. He demands the powder and arms be moved aft and the map be kept secret even from him, or he will resign.

scenes.title: An Uneasy Truce
scenes.summary: The doctor translates the demands as fear of mutiny, which Smollett formally denies while insisting on responsibility for safety. The squire angrily yields, and the doctor wryly declares Smollett and Silver the two honest men aboard.

scenes.title: Shifting Powder and Berths
scenes.summary: On deck the crew shifts powder aft and rebuilds the stern berths into a garrison. Silver arrives, questions the change, and is dismissed by the captain, who also coldly rebuffs Jim, deepening Jim's hatred of him.

scenes.title: Setting Sail
scenes.summary: Bustling night of loading and farewells gives way to dawn departure. The crew mans the capstan to Silver's sea shanty, the anchor comes up, and the Hispaniola begins her voyage, filling Jim with novelty and excitement shadowed by memory of the Admiral Benbow.

scenes.title: The Fall of Mr. Arrow
scenes.summary: The outward voyage is prosperous but marred by the disgrace of mate Mr. Arrow, who drinks himself useless from a mysterious supply and disappears overboard on a dark night. Job Anderson steps up as mate, supported by Trelawney and Israel Hands.

scenes.title: Barbecue in the Galley
scenes.summary: Jim describes the ship's cook Barbecue: crutch-bound yet agile, educated and brave, universally respected and kind to Jim. In the clean galley Silver spins yarns about his ancient swearing parrot Captain Flint, charming Jim into thinking him the best of men.

muse_override.reason: Warm galley camaraderie and humorous parrot tales create cozy joy with light adventure and hidden menace.

scenes.title: Spoiled Crew and Warning Foretold
scenes.summary: The squire and captain remain coldly at odds despite the ship's good qualities. The crew is spoiled with double grog, duff, and a free apple barrel, which the captain distrusts as making devils — yet that barrel will provide the warning that saves them from treachery.

scenes.title: The Last Day Outward
scenes.summary: On the last day of the outward voyage, the Hispaniola runs down with a steady breeze toward Treasure Island, all alow and aloft and everyone in the bravest spirits at being so near land.

scenes.title: Inside the Apple Barrel
scenes.summary: After sundown Jim slips on deck for an apple and climbs bodily into the nearly empty barrel, drowsing to the motion until Silver sits heavily against it, and he freezes, understanding all honest lives depend on what he overhears.

scenes.title: Silver's Flattery in the Apple Barrel
scenes.summary: Hidden in the apple barrel, Jim overhears Silver regaling a young seaman with pirate lore about Flint, Pew, and Roberts, and boasting of his saved fortune while flattering the lad into joining the gentlemen of fortune.

scenes.title: The Mutiny Plot Debated
scenes.summary: Israel Hands joins and presses for immediate mutiny, but Silver insists they wait until Smollett has sailed them there and the squire and doctor have found the treasure, then coldly votes for death for the honest party.

scenes.title: Terror, Rum, and Land Ho!
scenes.summary: Terror-stricken Jim nearly discovered when Silver sends Dick for an apple, is spared by a call for rum, learns faithful men remain aboard, and hears the lookout cry Land ho! as moonlight falls on the barrel.

scenes.title: Land Ho - The Island Sighted
scenes.summary: Roused by a rush on deck, Jim joins the crew as fog lifts with the moon to reveal the island ahead, while Captain Smollett alters course to clear it and questions the men.

muse_override.reason: Rushed deck gathering and fog-lifted island reveal blends lingering fear with wonder and adventure.

scenes.title: Silver's Smooth Pilot Talk
scenes.summary: Silver smoothly claims knowledge of the island as Skeleton Island and its anchorage, and passes Smollett's test with the altered chart despite his disappointment at the missing treasure marks.

scenes.title: A Friendly Threat
scenes.summary: Left shaken by what he overheard in the barrel, Jim endures Silver's creepily friendly talk of goats, bathing, and exploring before Silver hobbles below.

scenes.title: The Grog Ruse
scenes.summary: Jim secretly warns Livesey he has terrible news, prompting a ruse where Smollett praises the crew and orders grog so the officers can slip below and summon Jim unseen.

scenes.title: Council of War in the Cabin
scenes.summary: In the cabin Jim recounts Silver's mutiny plot, is toasted for his courage, and listens as the officers admit they are seven against nineteen and must bide time and watch.

scenes.title: First Sight of the Gloomy Island
scenes.summary: At dawn Jim comes on deck to see Treasure Island for the first time: grey melancholy woods, yellow sand-breaks, pines, and strange naked rock spires dominated by the Spy-glass. The Hispaniola rolls helplessly becalmed and Jim, queasy and empty-stomached, feels his heart sink and hates the very thought of the island despite bright sun and seabirds.

muse_override.reason: Gray melancholy woods, strange rock spires and pounding surf create foreboding mystery and sinking dread.

scenes.title: Warping Round With No Wind as Discipline Breaks
scenes.summary: With no wind, the crew must warp the ship for miles by boat around into the haven behind Skeleton Island in sweltering heat. Jim volunteers for a boat. Discipline collapses as the men grumble openly, Anderson worst of all. Long John Silver conns the ship through the narrow passage with perfect local knowledge.

scenes.title: Anchoring in the Silent Landlocked Haven
scenes.summary: They anchor in clean sand about a third of a mile from each shore, mainland on one side and Skeleton Island on the other. The anchor startles birds over the woods, then all falls silent again. The haven is entirely landlocked and buried in woods, ringed by distant hills, with swamps emptying in, and no sign of stockade to be seen.

scenes.title: Fever Smell and Threat of Mutiny
scenes.summary: The anchorage feels stagnant and poisonous, smelling of sodden leaves with surf booming outside; the doctor sniffs fever in the air. Aboard, mutiny hangs plainly over the growling, disobedient crew. Worst of all, Long John Silver anxiously bustles about smiling, singing, and smoothing things over, revealing how serious the danger is.

scenes.title: The Council and Offer of Shore Leave
scenes.summary: The officers hold a council in the cabin. The captain warns another order may trigger open mutiny and proposes trusting Silver to defuse it by granting the men an afternoon ashore. Loaded pistols are issued to the sure men, and the captain offers shore leave; the sullen crew instantly cheers, echoing off the hills.

scenes.title: Jim Stows Away and Flees Ashore
scenes.summary: Silver arranges the shore party as de facto captain while six men stay aboard. Seeing the cabin party does not need him, Jim impulsively hides in a boat's foresheets to go ashore. Noticed too late by Silver, Jim beats the other boat to the beach, swings into the trees, ignores Silver's shouts, and runs headlong into the thicket until he can run no more.

scenes.title: Joy of Exploration
scenes.summary: Jim slips away from Long John Silver and explores the island with delight, crossing marsh, sandy open ground, and twisted evergreen oaks beneath the Spy-glass hill.

scenes.title: Crawling to Overhear
scenes.summary: Alarmed by rising birds and approaching voices, Jim hides and crawls through the thicket to spy on Silver in earnest conversation with another sailor in a green dell.

scenes.title: Silver's Plea
scenes.summary: Silver appeals warmly to Tom to save his neck by joining the mutiny, while Tom, red-faced and shaking, refuses to turn against his duty.

scenes.title: Death Cry and Defiance
scenes.summary: A distant death-scream signals Alan's murder. Tom confronts Silver with the killing, renounces him as mate, and vows to die in his duty.

scenes.title: Tom Struck Down
scenes.summary: Tom turns his back on Silver and walks for the beach, but Silver hurls his crutch to strike him between the shoulders and then falls on him, stabbing him twice with his knife while Jim watches from ambush.

scenes.title: Faint Witnessed
scenes.summary: Jim reels and faints as the world spins away, then revives to find Silver composed again with crutch and hat, calmly cleaning his bloodstained knife on grass beside Tom's motionless body.

muse_override.reason: Fainting horror after witnessed murder blends shock, grief and lingering dread.

scenes.title: Panicked Flight
scenes.summary: Silver whistles for his comrades and Jim, fearing discovery as the next victim, flees in frenzy from the marsh toward the pines at the foot of the twin-peaked hill until a fresh alarm stops him.

scenes.title: The Figure in the Pines
scenes.summary: Fleeing the mutineers, Jim is startled by gravel and a dark, shaggy figure darting between pines. Feeling trapped between the murderers behind and this unknown creature ahead, he tries to outrun it, realizes it runs manlike on two legs, recalls cannibals, then takes courage from his pistol and walks resolutely toward it.

scenes.title: Poor Ben Gunn
scenes.summary: The wild man surprises Jim by kneeling in supplication. He names himself Ben Gunn, unspoken-with for three years. Jim sees a sun-blackened white man in patchwork canvas rags. Gunn explains he was marooned, has lived on goats, berries and oysters, and confesses a sore longing for Christian diet, especially cheese.

muse_override.reason: Lonely ragged castaway inspires wonder, mystery and pity with a touch of suspense.

scenes.title: Pious Boy Fallen and Rich
scenes.summary: Gunn perks up slyly at Jim's talk of getting aboard again, learns his name is Jim, tells of his pious mother and boyhood, his fall into roguery beginning on gravestones, and his return to piety on the lonely island, then whispers that he is rich.

scenes.title: Fear of Flint's Ship and Silver
scenes.summary: Jim takes Gunn for mad, but Gunn turns threatening and demands to know if the ship is Flint's; relieved to hear Flint is dead, he is alarmed to learn that Silver and some of Flint's hands are aboard.

scenes.title: The Confidence Told and the Thousand Pounds
scenes.summary: Jim tells Ben Gunn the whole story of the voyage and their predicament, winning his trust. Gunn offers to help if the squire will prove liberal to a thousand pounds and give him a passage home.

scenes.title: Flint's Burial and Gunn's Marooning
scenes.summary: Gunn recounts sailing in Flint's ship when the treasure was buried, Flint returning alone after murdering his six companions, and his own marooning three years ago with musket, spade, and pickaxe for urging a search, ending with a cryptic message for the squire to prove his identity.

scenes.title: Cannon and Flight to the Flag
scenes.summary: Talk of Gunn's hidden boat is cut short by cannon thunder from the anchorage, followed by small-arms fire. Jim cries they have begun to fight and runs toward the ships, with Gunn trotting beside him, guiding him left under the trees past his goat-killing ground and cemetery, until the Union Jack appears fluttering over the wood ahead.

muse_override.reason: Cannon thunder sparks urgent run toward the flag, mixing combat with adventurous suspense.

scenes.title: Helpless Council Aboard
scenes.summary: Aboard the windless Hispaniola, the captain, squire and doctor realize Jim has gone ashore with the mutineers. Sickened by the anchorage and alarmed for Jim, they decide Hunter and the doctor will go ashore for information.

scenes.title: The Stockade and the Death Cry
scenes.summary: Dodging the mutineers guarding the gigs, the doctor lands and finds the stockade with its log-house, palisade and precious spring. His hope turns to dread when a death-cry rings over the island and he fears for Jim.

scenes.title: Race to Provision the Blockhouse
scenes.summary: The doctor races back to the ship with a plan to seize the stockade for its water. Under armed threat to the mutineers below, the party loads the jolly-boat with arms, food and medicine and ferries stores ashore to provision the blockhouse.

scenes.title: Abandoning the Ship
scenes.summary: With the tide ebbing and voices approaching, the last party dumps spare arms overboard, loads the final boat, and coaxes Abraham Gray to defect after a scuffle below. They shove off, clear of the ship but not yet safe ashore.

scenes.title: Overloaded Against the Ebb
scenes.summary: The doctor narrates the fifth and final jolly-boat trip. Grossly overloaded with men and stores, the boat ships water while a strong ebb current sweeps them westward away from the stockade landing toward the pirates' gigs. Livesey steers upstream to fight the tide while Gray is quietly accepted as one of their own.

scenes.title: The Long Nine Revealed
scenes.summary: The mood snaps to horror as the crew remembers the long nine cannon. They watch Hands and four rogues strip its cover on the Hispaniola. Exposed broadside on their run for shore, they halt rowing so Trelawney can fire; his shot misses Hands but fells another pirate, provoking answering shouts as more pirates rush from the trees to the gigs.

scenes.title: Race for the Beach
scenes.summary: A desperate race for the beach begins. Only one gig is manned while the rest of the pirates try to cut them off by shore. Rowing hard despite the risk of swamping, the overloaded boat nears the sand as the crew watches anxiously for the cannon's match, knowing the gun is their only real danger.

scenes.title: Swamped and Wading Ashore
scenes.summary: At the squire's warning the captain backs water and the cannon fires in the same instant. The jolly-boat sinks gently by the stern in shallow water. No lives are lost but most powder, provisions, and three guns are drowned. Soaked and half-armed, with voices closing in the woods, they wade ashore fearing for Hunter and Joyce at the stockade.

scenes.title: Race to the Stockade
scenes.summary: The doctor's party sprints through the woods toward the stockade with pirates close behind, arms Trelawney and Gray, reaches the enclosure, and wins the first exchange of fire, killing one mutineer who is found shot through the heart.

scenes.title: Death of Tom Redruth
scenes.summary: A hidden pistol shot fells Tom Redruth; the party carries the dying gamekeeper into the log-house where he stoically asks forgiveness of the squire, asks for a prayer, and passes away.

scenes.title: Colors Raised and Stores Counted
scenes.summary: Smollett raises the British flag over the log-house, inventories their meager stores, drapes a flag over Tom's body to comfort the squire, then privately warns Livesey that rations are critically short.

muse_override.reason: Solemn flag over the dead and short rations blend mourning with looming scarcity.

scenes.title: Cannonade Under the Flag
scenes.summary: The ship opens cannon fire on the stockade; after debate about striking the flag, the defenders defiantly keep it flying and endure the evening bombardment as balls bury harmlessly in the sand.

scenes.title: Lost Stores and the Captain's Log
scenes.summary: Gray and Hunter attempt to recover the stranded pork at ebb tide but find mutineers under Silver already carrying it to the gigs; Smollett begins his log entry listing the faithful survivors and Livesey worries for Jim Hawkins.

scenes.title: Jim's Return
scenes.summary: A hail from the land side interrupts the gloom as Jim Hawkins appears alive, climbing over the stockade to rejoin the party.

muse_override.reason: Relief and joy at Jim's safe return dominate with surprise at the sudden hail.

scenes.title: Ben Gunn's Bargain in the Woods
scenes.summary: Jim resumes the narrative as Ben Gunn sees the Union Jack over the stockade and insists Jim's friends have won it. Ben detains Jim to pass his secret terms: a meeting alone with a gentleman on his word of honor, from noon to six bells, with promises of confidence and reasons of his own, and begs Jim not to betray him to Silver.

muse_override.reason: Secretive bargain with coded phrases and hidden motives creates mystery and suspense in the woods.

scenes.title: Cannonade and Watching the Pirates
scenes.summary: A cannonball interrupts the talk and both flee. Jim endures an hour-long bombardment from the ship, hiding through the woods, then creeps to the shore at sunset to watch the Hispaniola flying the Jolly Roger fire its last shot while drunken mutineers burn the jolly-boat and ferry to shore. He notes the white rock as a future landmark.

scenes.title: Return to the Stockade
scenes.summary: Jim regains the shoreward side of the stockade and is warmly welcomed by the faithful party. After telling his story, he looks over the log-house of unsquared pine with its raised floor, porch, and spring rising into a sunk ship's kettle.

muse_override.reason: Safe return and warm welcome with homely stockade detail creates calm relief with light joy.

scenes.title: The Empty Log-House
scenes.summary: Jim notes the bare interior with only a stone hearth and rusty fire-basket left, and surveys the cleared knoll where the stumps show the destroyed grove, with moss and ferns surviving only along the streamlet and dense wood pressing close outside.

muse_override.reason: Abandoned hearth and ruined grove create desolate, mysterious calm.

scenes.title: Sand, Smoke, and the Dead
scenes.summary: Cold wind drives sand through every chink and smoke from the roof-hole chokes the house, while Gray sits with his face bandaged from his break with the mutineers and poor Tom Redruth lies unburied and stark under the Union Jack.

scenes.title: Watches Set and Talk of Cheese
scenes.summary: Smollett rouses everyone from despair by dividing them into watches and setting tasks for wood, burial, cooking, and sentry duty. At the door, the doctor praises Smollett and questions Jim about Ben Gunn, laughing that island solitude explains his strangeness and promising his hidden Parmesan cheese for Ben.

muse_override.reason: Weary camp duties and grave-digging softened by kindly leadership and cheese humor sustain calm recovery.

scenes.title: Burial and Council of War
scenes.summary: The party buries Tom in the sand, eats pork and grog, and the leaders confer. With stores low, their plan is to whittle down the fifteen remaining buccaneers while counting rum and marsh sickness as allies, hoping the pirates will sail away.

scenes.title: Sleep Broken by Silver Himself
scenes.summary: Dead tired, Jim sleeps like a log while the others rise early to gather wood. He is jolted awake by cries of a flag of truce and the shock that Silver himself is coming.

scenes.title: Flag of Truce on a Cold Morning
scenes.summary: At dawn on a cold, misty, unhealthy morning, Jim spots Silver with a companion waving a flag of truce outside the stockade. Captain Smollett suspects a trick and posts Doctor Livesey, Jim, and Gray to loopholes while ordering all hands to load muskets.

scenes.title: Silver Comes Inside to Parley
scenes.summary: Smollett demands Silver's business and denies knowing him as captain. Silver claims command after the captain's desertion and asks safe passage for a parley. He climbs laboriously over the stockade fence and up the knoll in his best coat, trading cold insults with Smollett before sitting to talk.

scenes.title: Terms for the Chart
scenes.summary: Silver admits the night attack shook his men and demands the treasure chart in exchange for sparing lives. Jim realizes Ben Gunn must have visited the pirates' camp. Smollett refuses to betray Gray, and the two leaders smoke in tense silence before Silver offers divided stores and rescue by a passing ship if the chart is surrendered.

scenes.title: Ultimatum and Furious Departure
scenes.summary: Smollett rejects Silver utterly, ordering the pirates to surrender one by one for trial in England or be killed, insisting they cannot find the treasure, sail the ship, or win a fight. Enraged, refused help to rise, Silver hauls himself up, curses them, spits in the spring, vows to stove in the blockhouse within the hour, and stumbles back to the woods.

muse_override.reason: Defiant ultimatum and furious threat create tense standoff with imminent attack, dominated by suspense and brewing combat.

scenes.title: Quarters and Battle Plan
scenes.summary: Immediately after Silver leaves, Smollett rebukes the crew for abandoning posts, praises Gray, then organizes the blockhouse defense, stockpiling muskets, dousing the fire, and assigning each man to door and loopholes.

scenes.title: The Tense Wait and First Shot
scenes.summary: Sweltering in the blockhouse, the defenders wait anxiously through a dull hour until Joyce spots movement, fires, and provokes a scattering but harmless volley from the woods.

scenes.title: Counting Shots
scenes.summary: After the volley misses, Smollett questions the men to count shots from each side and concludes the main attack will come from the north, but keeps all posts guarded.

scenes.title: Boarders Over the Palisade
scenes.summary: With a huzza the pirates rush the north stockade, swarm over under covering fire, seize loopholes and burst into the doorway, reversing the fight and filling the log-house with smoke and confusion.

scenes.title: Out and Fight Them in the Open
scenes.summary: Smollett orders everyone out with cutlasses; Hawkins, the doctor, and Gray fight hand-to-hand around the house, cutting down or driving off the boarders until the woods are empty again.

scenes.title: The Price of Victory
scenes.summary: Rushing back to cover, the defenders find Joyce killed, Hunter stunned, and the captain wounded, while Smollett takes grim comfort that five pirates fallen has improved their odds.

scenes.title: After the Battle
scenes.summary: Quiet aftermath inside the blockhouse after repulsing the mutineers; the survivors tend the wounded and eat dinner amid groans, learning Hunter is dying and the captain, though badly hurt, will recover.

scenes.title: The Doctor Leaves Alone for the Woods
scenes.summary: After consulting with the squire and captain, Doctor Livesey arms himself with pistols, cutlass, musket, and the chart and leaves alone over the north palisade into the woods. Gray is thunderstruck and fears the doctor is mad, while Jim guesses he is going to see Ben Gunn. Stifling heat, clinging resin, blood, and dead bodies fill Jim with disgust and envy of the doctor in the cool woods.

muse_override.reason: Doctor's lone departure puzzles the men, mixing suspense and mystery with bold adventure.

scenes.title: Jim Deserts to Find the Boat
scenes.summary: Disgusted while cleaning the blockhouse, Jim resolves on his escapade, filling his pockets with biscuit and taking pistols, powder, and bullets. Planning to find Ben Gunn's boat by the white rock on the sandy spit, he seizes the moment while the squire and Gray tend the captain, bolts over the stockade into the trees, and leaves only two sound men to guard the house.

scenes.title: Watching the Anchorage
scenes.summary: Jim treks the east coast in surf and sea-breeze to the spit ridge, watching the anchorage in fog where the Hispaniola flies the Jolly Roger, hearing Silver's men laughing before Flint's parrot screams and their boat pulls for shore at sunset.

scenes.title: The Coracle Found
scenes.summary: Crawling to the white rock in near-dark, Jim finds a hidden hollow with a goatskin tent and discovers Ben Gunn's tiny, light homemade coracle.

muse_override.reason: Nighttime crawling discovery of the hidden goatskin boat evokes mystery, adventure, and wonder.

scenes.title: Night Resolve to Cut Her Adrift
scenes.summary: Emboldened by the find, Jim resolves under foggy black night to cut the Hispaniola adrift to stop the mutineers sailing away, eats, shoulders the coracle, and launches it through ebb and swampy sand guided by the pirates' fire and the ship's cabin light.

muse_override.reason: Stealthy night fog mission to cut the ship adrift is tense, secretive adventure.

scenes.title: Drifting Down to the Hispaniola
scenes.summary: Jim struggles to control the lopsided coracle, but the ebb tide carries him down toward the anchored Hispaniola until he seizes her taut hawser in the dark.

scenes.title: Waiting to Cut the Hawser
scenes.summary: Jim realizes cutting the taut hawser would be dangerously violent, so he waits until a southwest puff slacks the rope and then saws through most of its strands.

scenes.title: Drunken Quarrel and Campfire Song
scenes.summary: While waiting, Jim listens to Hands and the red-nightcap man drunkenly quarreling in the cabin and watches the campfire ashore where pirates drone a doleful sailor's song.

scenes.title: Cast Adrift and a Glimpse of Murder
scenes.summary: Jim cuts the last fibers, is swept against the bows, then hauls himself along a trailing line to peer through the cabin window and sees Hands and his mate locked throat-to-throat in a deadly wrestle.

scenes.title: Swept Out to Sea
scenes.summary: The chorus ashore gives way to alarm as the current whirls schooner and coracle southward through the narrows; Jim lies flat expecting breakers and death until exhaustion sinks him into sleep.

scenes.title: A Hostile Lee Shore
scenes.summary: Jim awakes adrift in the coracle off the southwest end of the island and tries to land near Haulbowline Head, but pounding surf, cliffs, and barking sea lions convince him the shore is deadly.

scenes.title: Choosing the Cape of the Woods
scenes.summary: Carried by the northward current, Jim decides to leave Haulbowline Head behind and save his strength to attempt a landing on the kindlier-looking Cape of the Woods.

scenes.title: Riding the Swell
scenes.summary: Jim learns the touchy coracle rides the smooth swell safely only if left undisturbed, and lying low he nudges her shoreward with weak paddle strokes while suffering burning thirst as the current carries him past the cape.

scenes.title: The Hispaniola Sighted
scenes.summary: Adrift and thirsty in the coracle, Jim sights the Hispaniola under full sail less than half a mile away and watches in surprise as she bears down and then is taken dead aback with shivering sails.

scenes.title: No Hand at the Helm
scenes.summary: Watching the schooner fall off and come helpless into the wind again and again, Jim realizes no one is steering her and hopes the men are drunk or deserted so he might board and return her to the captain.

muse_override.reason: Ghost ship tacking aimlessly with flapping sails builds suspenseful mystery about vanished crew.

scenes.title: Paddling After the Drifting Schooner
scenes.summary: Seeing the current carry both craft alike and the unsteered schooner hanging in irons, Jim is tempted by thirst and adventure to sit up and paddle hard after the Hispaniola.

scenes.title: Leap to the Jib-Boom
scenes.summary: Gaining through calms and losing to wind and leeway, Jim seizes his chance as the schooner bears down on him and leaps from the swamped coracle to catch the jib-boom.

scenes.title: Boarding the Deserted Schooner
scenes.summary: Jim clambers along the bowsprit as the jib slams over, nearly throwing him off. He crawls back to the deck to find it deserted, then the boom swings inboard and reveals the afterdeck.

scenes.title: The Bloody Afterdeck
scenes.summary: Jim discovers the two watchmen bloody and fallen: Red-cap stiff and grinning in death, Hands pale and sinking against the bulwark. As the ship bucks, Jim realizes they fought each other drunk, then Hands moans and stirs alive.

scenes.title: Ransacked Cabin and Brandy
scenes.summary: Jim ironically greets the wounded Hands, who can only beg for brandy. Jim dodges the boom to the ransacked cabin and empty cellar, then returns with brandy for Hands and food and water for himself.

muse_override.reason: Ransacked cabin, drunken wreckage and hurried search create tense suspenseful mystery.

scenes.title: Captain Hawkins Strikes the Jolly Roger
scenes.summary: Over his meal Jim declares himself captain come to take possession of the ship. He hauls down the black flag and throws it overboard, hailing the king and an end to Captain Silver.

muse_override.reason: Triumphant boy-captain striking the black flag is pure adventurous joy.

scenes.title: A Bargain to Sail Her
scenes.summary: Hands, watching slyly, proposes a bargain: food, drink and a bandage for his wound in exchange for telling Jim how to sail. Jim insists on beaching at North Inlet, and Hands eagerly agrees he has no choice.

scenes.title: Running for North Inlet
scenes.summary: With the tiller lashed, Jim binds Hands' stabbed thigh and gets the Hispaniola sailing easily toward the north point. Elated by sun, speed and conquest, Jim is still chilled by Hands' derisive, treacherous watching smile.

scenes.title: Laying To with a Wounded Man
scenes.summary: Becalmed off North Inlet waiting for tide, Jim shares a quiet meal with the wounded Hands, whose talk about the dead shipmate and spirits turns ominous as he tries to send Jim below for wine.

scenes.title: The Hidden Dirk
scenes.summary: Sensing deception, Jim slips around to spy and watches Hands crawl to the scuppers, arm himself with a bloodstained dirk, and hide it, confirming Jim is meant to be the victim after the beaching.

scenes.title: Wine, Pretense, and Tobacco
scenes.summary: Jim returns with wine; Hands feigns weakness, drinks to luck, and begs Jim to cut him tobacco as if dying.

scenes.title: Sin, Defiance, and Orders
scenes.summary: Jim urges repentance for broken trust and murder; Hands defends his ruthless creed, then drops the act to order Jim to sail into the anchorage.

scenes.title: Threading the Narrow Entrance
scenes.summary: With Hands piloting and Jim at the helm, the Hispaniola threads the narrow, shoal east-west entrance to North Inlet, then opens the long river-like anchorage with its flower-covered, seaweed-hung wreck proving calm water.

muse_override.reason: Delicate shaving-the-banks piloting blends suspense and adventure resolving into calm at the sheltered wreck anchorage.

scenes.title: Driving Her Stem-On for Shore
scenes.summary: Hands chooses a flat sandy beaching place, explains floating her off again with a line to the pines at high water, then talks Jim through the helm orders until Jim luffs and drives the Hispaniola stem-on for shore.

scenes.title: Knife Attack on Deck
scenes.summary: Distracted by the beaching, Jim turns to find Hands charging with the dirk; saved by the swinging tiller, he flees forward with a misfired pistol and dodges around the mainmast.

muse_override.reason: Desperate dodging of Hands' dirk around the mast is pure close combat charged with life-or-death suspense.

scenes.title: Capsize and Flight to the Crosstrees
scenes.summary: The Hispaniola strikes and heels hard to port, hurling Jim and Hands into the scuppers. Jim springs into the mizzen shrouds and reaches the crosstrees as Hands's dirk misses below him. While Hands climbs painfully with the dirk in his teeth, Jim reprimes one pistol and reloads the other, then holds him off at gunpoint as Hands offers to strike.

scenes.title: Thrown Dirk and Fall into the Water
scenes.summary: Mid-surrender talk, Hands throws his dirk and pins Jim by the shoulder to the mast. In pain and surprise both of Jim's pistols go off, and Hands looses his grasp and plunges headfirst into the water.

scenes.title: Hands Sunk Beside the Ship
scenes.summary: From the crosstrees Jim watches Hands rise once in foam and blood, then sink to lie huddled on the bright sand in the ship's shadow, dead by shot and drowning and left as food for fishes.

muse_override.reason: Somber underwater death with lingering dread after combat, calm water over corpse.

scenes.title: Pinned to the Mast and Set Free
scenes.summary: Certain Hands is dead, Jim is overcome by sickness, bleeding, and horror of falling beside the coxswain; pinned by the dirk, he tears free by a shudder and jerk, and regains the deck by the starboard shrouds.

scenes.title: O'Brien Overboard Beside Israel
scenes.summary: Below Jim tends his slight shoulder wound, then as master of the ship heaves O'Brien's corpse overboard, watching him settle beside Israel on the bottom with fishes steering over both.

scenes.title: Securing the Schooner at Sunset
scenes.summary: Alone on the captured Hispaniola as tide turns and evening shadows and breeze rise, Jim sees danger in the sails. He douses the jibs, cuts the mainsail halyards, then wades ashore through shallow water, leaving the schooner canted on her side.

muse_override.reason: Quiet sunset beauty is overtaken by the listing ship and desperate cutting loose, leaving tense uncertain suspense.

scenes.title: Off the Sea to Boast
scenes.summary: Elated at leaving the sea with the Hispaniola cleared of buccaneers, Jim sets his face homeward for the stockade to boast of his feat, crossing open wood and wading mid-calf through the small easterly stream.

scenes.title: Wary Approach by Moonrise
scenes.summary: Near Ben Gunn's country Jim grows circumspect at the sight of the maroon's fire, stumbles through deepening darkness, then hurries on by the rising moon toward the stockade, slowing warily for fear of being shot by his own party.

scenes.title: The Red Fire at the Blockhouse
scenes.summary: By moonlight Jim comes to the edge of the clearing and is baffled by a red, smoldering glow that proves to be an immense fire burned to embers beside the dark, silent blockhouse.

muse_override.reason: Quiet moonlit clearing with unexplained red embers creates mystery and suspense with no action yet.

scenes.title: False Reassurance in the Dark
scenes.summary: Alarmed by the wasteful fire, Jim steals over the palisade and crawls to the house, then is reassured by his friends snoring loudly inside, condemns their bad watch, and slips in through the dark doorway.

scenes.title: Pieces of Eight - Captured by Silver
scenes.summary: Silver's parrot shrieks 'Pieces of eight!' betraying Jim. The sleepers spring up, Silver demands who goes, Jim is seized while trying to flee, and Silver orders a torch to be brought.

scenes.title: In the Enemy's Camp
scenes.summary: Jim enters the blockhouse to find the pirates in possession and his friends gone, fears them dead. Silver greets him with false friendliness and tells him he cannot go back to his own party and must join with Captain Silver.

scenes.title: The Doctor's Bargain
scenes.summary: Relieved his friends are alive, Jim presses for answers. Silver explains the doctor came with a flag of truce, traded stores, blockhouse and supplies after the ship vanished, and claimed Jim was abandoned and not part of the treaty, forcing Jim to choose.

scenes.title: Defiance and Protection
scenes.summary: Jim defiantly confesses he overheard the plot in the apple barrel, cut the schooner adrift and killed aboard her, offering to save them at trial if spared. Morgan moves to kill him, but Silver furiously asserts his captaincy and forbids any hand laid on the boy.

scenes.title: The Council Called
scenes.summary: A tense standoff leaves Silver watching his muttering men as they huddle, invoke their rights, and file out one by one for a forecastle council, leaving Silver and Jim alone with the torch.

scenes.title: Back to Back Bargain
scenes.summary: Alone, Silver drops the act and whispers that both are near death and deposed, pledging to stand by Jim back-to-back if Jim will save his neck. He declares himself now on the squire's side, suspects Jim hid the ship, and puzzles over why the doctor gave him the treasure chart.

scenes.title: Watching in the Dark
scenes.summary: Alone in the dark blockhouse, Jim and Silver wait as the mutineer council outside borrows a torch. Jim watches through the loophole as the men gather with knife and book to prepare the Black Spot.

scenes.title: The Black Spot Delivered
scenes.summary: The deputation enters and hands Silver the Black Spot cut from a Bible and marked Deposed. Silver mocks their sacrilege and asserts his rights as captain to hear grievances and reply before any vote.

scenes.title: The Four Charges Against Silver
scenes.summary: George Merry lays four charges against Silver — bungling the cruise, letting the enemy out of the trap, refusing to attack on the march, and protecting Jim. Silver calmly answers the first point, blaming George, Anderson, and Hands for crossing him and losing the Hispaniola.

scenes.title: Silver Reclaims Command with the Chart
scenes.summary: Silver answers the remaining charges, defending Jim as a hostage and his bargain for the doctor's care, then flourishes Flint's treasure chart. The sight turns the crew, who cheer Silver and restore him as captain.

muse_override.reason: Silver faces down mutiny then flips dread to triumph by revealing the treasure chart.

scenes.title: Aftermath and Uneasy Sleep
scenes.summary: With the mutiny quelled, the spoiled Bible leaf is examined and dismissed. The men drink and sleep while Jim lies awake pondering Silver's double game to hold the crew and save his own life.

scenes.title: The Doctor's Morning Visit
scenes.summary: At dawn the doctor hails the blockhouse from the woods. Silver greets him jovially and reveals Jim as a new lodger, shocking Livesey who pauses before insisting on duty first and entering to see the sick.

scenes.title: Mutineers' Doctor
scenes.summary: Fearless among the mutineers, Livesey makes his professional rounds, teasing and dosing his patients who submit humbly. He finishes and asks to speak with Jim.

scenes.title: Parole Through the Stockade
scenes.summary: George Merry angrily refuses the talk, but Silver silences him, takes Jim's word of honor not to escape, and arranges a parley through the stockade. He quells the pirates' accusations of double-dealing and slowly leads Jim out to the doctor.

scenes.title: Silver Pleads for Mercy
scenes.summary: Alone outside with his back to his men, a trembling Silver begs Livesey to speak him fair and remember the good he has done, for both his life and the boy's are at stake. He then withdraws out of earshot to whistle and watch.

scenes.title: Jim's Confession of the Ship
scenes.summary: Left alone, the doctor reproaches Jim for desertion until Jim weeps and fears torture. Livesey urges escape, but Jim refuses to break his word and instead confesses he has recovered the ship and hidden her in North Inlet.

scenes.title: Warning and Farewell
scenes.summary: Silver returns and Livesey cryptically warns him not to hurry after the treasure and to look out for squalls when he finds it. He promises to do his best short of perjury to save Silver if they live, tells him to keep Jim close and halloo for help, then shakes hands and leaves into the wood.

muse_override.reason: Tense farewell with veiled warning and secret plot creates suspense and mystery with sad parting.

scenes.title: Silver's Private Pact
scenes.summary: Alone together, Silver thanks Jim for refusing to run and saving his life, proposing they stick back-to-back through the coming treasure-hunt under sealed orders to save their necks.

scenes.title: Breakfast Boast
scenes.summary: Around a wasteful, roaring breakfast fire, Silver flatters and reassures the pirates, claiming they hold the advantage with the boats once treasure is found and that Jim will be kept as gold for safety and later rewarded.

muse_override.reason: Wasteful pirate camp and Silver's cunning boasting create tense adventurous suspense.

scenes.title: Jim's Uneasy Dread
scenes.summary: Jim sinks into dread at Silver's double treachery and the prospect of fighting five seamen with a cripple, haunted by his friends' desertion of the stockade, the ceded chart, and the doctor's warning about squalls.

scenes.title: March and Crossing
scenes.summary: Roped like a dancing bear behind armed Silver, Jim marches with the pick-and-provision laden party to the damaged gigs, crosses the anchorage debating Flint's ambiguous chart marks, and lands to climb toward the plateau.

scenes.title: Pleasant Ascent
scenes.summary: Climbing from miry marsh into open pine, nutmeg, and scented broom, the fanned-out party enjoys fresh air and sunshine while Jim stays back to help the panting Silver over sliding gravel.

scenes.title: Skeleton Compass
scenes.summary: A terrified shout halts the climb at a skeleton laid straight under a pine, feet one way and hands raised like a diver, which Silver proves by compass bears E.S.E. by E toward Skeleton Island.

scenes.title: Flint's Pointer Terror
scenes.summary: Silver declares the yellow-haired bones Allardyce, a murdered pointer laid by Flint, and as the men note missing knife and money and recall Flint's horrible death and song, Silver urges on for doubloons while hushed terror keeps them bunched together.

muse_override.reason: Compass skeleton and Flint ghost talk spread cold dread and mystery.

scenes.title: Rest on the Brow
scenes.summary: The treasure party rests on the brow of the ascent to rest Silver and the sick. They gaze over a vast, silent panorama of surf, islands, and the Spy-glass. Silver takes bearings toward the tall trees, while talk turns uneasily to Flint in low whispers.

muse_override.reason: Quiet rest atop the hill with vast solitary seascape and uneasy talk of dead Flint blends calm with lurking suspense.

scenes.title: The Voice Among the Trees
scenes.summary: A thin trembling voice sings Flint's song from the trees, then wails for Darby M'Graw to fetch rum. The pirates turn ashen with supernatural terror and stand rooted, convinced it is Flint's ghost.

scenes.title: It Was Ben Gunn
scenes.summary: Silver fights his own fear to rally the men, arguing a spirit would have no echo. The men seize on the idea it is Ben Gunn, alive or dead, whom nobody fears. Courage and color return and they set off again with the compass.

muse_override.reason: Superstitious terror of Flint's ghost dissolves into relieved courage when revealed as Ben Gunn's echo.

scenes.title: The Open Summit to the Third Tree
scenes.summary: The party crosses the open summit in heat, Dick clinging fearfully to his Bible and sickening with fever while Silver mocks him, passing the first two tall trees as wrong before reaching the giant third tree.

muse_override.reason: Open sunlit trek toward the towering landmark mixes adventure with uneasy sickness and dread.

scenes.title: Gold Fever and Murder Foreseen
scenes.summary: Nearing the treasure, gold fever consumes the pirates while Jim reads murder in Silver's eyes as he plans to seize the gold and kill, and recalls Flint murdering his six accomplices on this very plateau.

scenes.title: The Empty Cache
scenes.summary: Rushing the last thicket with a huzza, the leaders stop dead with a low cry. Before them lies an old rifled excavation with a broken pick and Walrus-branded cases: the cache has been found and the seven hundred thousand pounds are gone.

muse_override.reason: Stunned halt at the rifled cache mixes loss, shock and tense mystery.

scenes.title: The Empty Pit
scenes.summary: The treasure pit is empty except for a single two-guinea piece. Silver instantly masters his disappointment while the other mutineers turn furious. Silver pulls Jim to his side across the pit and trades defiant insults with Merry as the five gather opposite them in a tense standoff.

scenes.title: Ambush at the Excavation
scenes.summary: Merry rallies the mutineers to rush Silver and Jim, but three shots from ambush in the thicket kill Merry and the bandaged man and scatter the rest. Silver finishes Merry with his pistol as the doctor, Gray, and Ben Gunn emerge with smoking muskets.

scenes.title: Race for the Boats
scenes.summary: The party races to cut the surviving mutineers off from the boats. Silver struggles heroically on his crutch to keep up. Finding the survivors fleeing toward Mizzenmast Hill, they rest while Silver thanks the doctor and awkwardly greets Ben Gunn.

muse_override.reason: Frantic chase to cut off the boats eases into breathless relief and surprise at Ben Gunn.

scenes.title: How Ben Gunn Found and Hid the Treasure
scenes.summary: Walking downhill to the boats, the doctor relates how Ben Gunn, wandering the island, found the skeleton and the treasure, dug it up with his pickax, and carried it to his cave on the two-pointed hill months before the Hispaniola arrived.

muse_override.reason: Ben Gunn's lonely discovery and secret hoarding blends mystery, adventure and wonder.

scenes.title: How the Doctor Traded the Useless Chart
scenes.summary: The doctor explains trading the now-useless chart and stores to Silver for safe passage to the cave to guard the money, ambushing the mutineers at the pine with Gray and Ben Gunn, and Silver remarks he owes his life to Jim's presence.

muse_override.reason: Doctor's cunning explanation resolves tension with relieved, adventurous revelation.

scenes.title: Recovery of the Hispaniola
scenes.summary: The party rows the long way round to North Inlet, passing Ben Gunn's cave where the squire waves. Inside the inlet they joyfully recover the drifted Hispaniola, re-anchor her, and land at Rum Cove while Gray returns to guard the ship.

muse_override.reason: Cheerful relief at finding Hispaniola intact makes joyful adventure dominant.

scenes.title: The Squire Rebukes Silver
scenes.summary: At the cave mouth the squire greets Jim kindly but confronts Silver with cold condemnation, calling him villain and impostor whose dead victims hang about his neck, while Silver accepts it with humble politeness.

muse_override.reason: Tense moral confrontation and verbal rebuke, not physical battle, with grief for the dead.

scenes.title: Treasure and Supper in the Cave
scenes.summary: Inside the firelit cave Jim beholds Flint's vast heaps of coin and gold bars. Captain Smollett welcomes Jim coolly and questions Silver's return to duty. The friends share a gay, happy supper of salted goat and ship's wine with Silver quietly obsequious on the edge of the light.

scenes.title: Hauling the Treasure
scenes.summary: With a sentry watching the remaining mutineers, the small crew works for days carrying gold to the beach, boating it to the Hispaniola, and sorting a vast, varied hoard of coins in the cave.

scenes.title: Voices from the Darkness
scenes.summary: On a night stroll above the lowlands, Jim and the doctor hear shrieking and singing from the marooned mutineers below. Silver intrudes uninvited, and the doctor rebukes him while declaring he would risk himself to aid them if they are raving with fever.

scenes.title: Deserted on the Island
scenes.summary: After the doctor's sharp retort to Silver, the party hears no more of the three pirates but a distant shot. A council resolves to desert them on the island, leaving powder, food, medicines, tools, clothing, and tobacco.

muse_override.reason: Relieved merciful farewell brings calm joy as the adventure quietly closes.

scenes.title: Farewell to the Island
scenes.summary: Loaded at last, the Hispaniola sails from North Inlet; the three abandoned men kneel pleading on a sand spit, then fire a parting shot, until Treasure Island sinks below the horizon.

muse_override.reason: Bittersweet sailing away blends adventurous relief with pity for the marooned men and a last tense shot.

scenes.title: Safe Harbor and Silver's Escape
scenes.summary: Short-handed and battered by gales, the crew reaches a welcoming port in Spanish America; ashore for the night, they return to learn Ben Gunn helped Silver escape with a sack of coin, a loss all are glad to accept.

scenes.title: Safe Home and Shares
scenes.summary: The Hispaniola makes Bristol with only five survivors, and the treasure is shared; Smollett retires, Gray rises to mate and family man, and Ben Gunn squanders his thousand pounds and settles as a lodge-keeper.

muse_override.reason: Peaceful homecoming and fair shares bring calm contentment and gentle joy with faint nostalgia for lost crew.

scenes.title: Silver Lost and Haunting Dreams
scenes.summary: Silver disappears from Jim's life for good, the remaining hoard is left buried, and Jim is left with nightmares of surf and Captain Flint's cry of pieces of eight.
